idea: "What's Missing?" #3 (THE LIBRARY, story corner, at a small wooden easel): Baby Jimmy's toddler crayon drawing of a SNOWMAN comes alive and wiggles on the paper – but it has NO NOSE ('Oh no! My snowman has no nose!'); 'Two round eyes and a big smile...'; Jimmy points at the empty spot and asks the viewer 'What's missing? Hmm?' (2 s pause) – 'A nose! A nose! An orange nose!'; 'Magic crayon, draw with me! A carrot nose!' – he draws an orange carrot nose; chorus 'Snowman, snowman! Here's your nose!'; review 'Eyes, a smile and a carrot nose! Yay!'; copy-me 'Wiggle, wiggle, like a snowman! Brrr, brrr! So cold!'. Loop: the hook framing again, the snowman now with its carrot nose, bye-bye wave 'Happy snowman! Bye bye, friends!'.
title: Oh No! My Snowman Has No Nose! ⛄ What's Missing? | Learn with Baby Jimmy | Crayon Babies
description:
Oh no! Baby Jimmy's crayon snowman has two round eyes and a big smile… but something is missing! Can you spot it? Look closely, shout the answer, and help Jimmy fix his snowman with the Magic Crayon!

🎬 What happens in this video:
😮 "Oh no! My snowman has no nose!"
👀 Two round eyes and a big smile…
🤔 "What's missing?" – look closely and shout the answer!
🥕 A nose! An orange carrot nose!
🖍️ "Magic crayon, draw with me!"
⛄ Wiggle like a snowman – brrr, so cold! Bye bye, friends!

📚 Kids learn: spot what's missing • nose • snowman • carrot • orange • eyes and smile

🎶 Voices only: children singing, humming and clapping with a soft hand drum – no other musical instruments.

A fun winter "What's Missing?" sing-along for toddlers and preschoolers: Baby Jimmy finds that his crayon snowman drawing has no nose, little viewers spot the missing part, and the Magic Crayon draws an orange carrot nose so the snowman is happy again.
